# SaveTexture 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Textures](Blitz3D-Textures)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SaveTexture:Int32 texture:Int32, file:String, frame:Int32=0, settings:String=\
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `texture` | Int32 | required | The texture. |
| `file` | String | required | The path of the file to write. |
| `frame` | Int32 | `0` | The frame to save. Defaults to 0. |
| `settings` | String | `\` | How to encode the file, such as `"quality=85"`. Defaults to an empty string. |

**Returns:** 1 if the file was written, otherwise 0 (also for a frame that the texture does not have). With [AsyncSaving](AsyncSaving) on, 1 means that the save was queued, see [SavesFailed](SavesFailed).

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Writes one frame of a texture into a picture file, the same as saving its [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer) with [SaveBuffer](SaveBuffer). The format comes from the end of the file name (`.bmp`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp`, `.jxl`, `.tga`, any other name is a BMP), and the optional `settings` choose how the file is made, see [Saving pictures](Saving-Pictures).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
tex = CreateTexture(64, 64)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(tex)
Color 255, 128, 0
Rect 0, 0, 64, 64, 1
Color 255, 255, 255
Oval 8, 8, 48, 48, 1
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
If SaveTexture(tex, "texture.png") Then Print "texture.png written" Else Print "could not save"
SaveTexture tex, "texture.jpg", 0, "quality=95,subsampling=444"
WaitKey
```

This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals can only save buffers and images.
